title: Storytelling and Animation
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Creative Arts and Sports; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts and Sports teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use oral narratives from local communities; flipbooks from small notebooks.

skills.key_step: The child names storytelling techniques (voice variation, gesture, facial expression, pauses, audience participation) and the qualities of a good flipbook (many pages, small changes, same place).

floor.prerequisite: Has put on a puppet show (Grade 5).
floor.question: Which way should a puppet face?

steps: Tell the story with voice changes.
For a flipbook, change each page a little.
contexts: an animation for a class message

board.do: The storyteller stops before the ending.

misconceptions.repair: Tell one line in a flat voice and then as the hyena; ask which holds attention.

misconceptions.ask: What does a good flipbook have?
misconceptions.repair: Flip a ten-page flipbook of a bouncing ball.

misconceptions.ask: How can a storyteller involve the audience?
misconceptions.repair: Use a call-and-response opening the class answers.

misconceptions.ask: In a flipbook, should each page change a lot or a little?
misconceptions.repair: Flip two books, big changes and small; compare.

checks.question: Name one storytelling technique.
checks.answer: any of: voice variation, gesture, facial expression, pause, audience participation

checks.question: What makes flipbook movement smooth?
checks.answer: small changes from page to page
